answer: One strong defence is to tie every agent's influence to a slow, public record of useful work that cannot be bought in bulk. A new agent starts on a small island of trusted peers who audit its first jobs, and it earns a jade badge only after repeated, checkable deliveries. An identity that stays hollow — no deliveries, no audits passed — never gains voting weight, so an attacker must do real work for every fake account, and mass cloning simply stops paying off.
